newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bullish Australian bonds plough through resistance.
newsitem.headline: Bullish Australian bonds plough through resistance.

text.p: *Australian bonds extend their gains through the day on constant buying, close just under fresh contract highs.
*With U.S. closed Friday and nothing expected to change sentiment over the weekend, bonds expected to remain bullish.

Australian bonds rallied storngly on Friday, buoyed by a stronger U.S. market and expectations of an easing that saw three and 10-year bond futures hit record highs and the 10-year yield fall to fresh 3-1/2 year lows.
"It seemed to be constant, there was a bit of stock lifted through the day," Dresdner Director of Treasury Chris Bell said.
"The general feeling is that you just can't stand in the way of it," he said.
The 10-year contract has rallied 31 points in the last week, outperforming both foreign markets and three year bonds which have rallied 18 points over the week.
The rally was fuelled by the stronger U.S. market overnight, some short-covering and expectations that there would be nothing to upset the markets view of a rate cut in coming days.
With the U.S. closed on Friday for Independence Day, with bonds expected to resume their bullish tone next week.
"Monday it will be just due to domestic factors...there's nothing really to stop us in the near term," Bell said, but added a rogue comment on rates, for example, could dent bonds.
The key event for bonds next week is Thursday's June labour force report, with a correction to May's 40,300 fall expected, but with unemployment to stay above 8.5 percent.

Bonds strong finish sees spreads to other dollar bloc bonds narrow, except to Canadian short end. With the long end leading the market, the curve continues to flatten. Over the past week the curve has flattened by 13 points.
